memory_update.text: STRA is the cleanest US-listed reference name for accredited adult online universities plus employer education-benefit distribution via Capella, Strayer, Workforce Edge, and Sophia Learning.

NNI should be tracked as an underfollowed supplier/platform candidate because its Education Technology Services and Payments segment may benefit from institutional tuition payment plans and education workflows without owning schools.

LRN provides adjacent exposure to adult professional skills training and enterprise talent development, but needs segment-level validation because core investor perception and revenue may remain K-12-weighted.

LINC is a plausible employer-aligned workforce-pathway operator for skilled trades; online-degree purity is weaker, so it should remain underfollowed/adjacent until employer-partner economics are verified.

Layer 1C should search for smaller suppliers around enrollment marketing, student success/retention software, education-benefit administration, credential data, LMS, assessment/proctoring, and tuition/payment rails; many may be private or hidden inside broader SaaS/payment companies.

node: Adult online universities and corporate-partner degree/certificate pathways
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a compact US-listed universe around adult online universities, employer-affiliated degree pathways, workforce certificates, institutional payments, and career-training platforms. STRA is the clearest direct reference asset owner because its US higher-education segment includes Capella and Strayer, while its ETS segment explicitly manages employer education-benefit relationships. LRN and LINC provide adjacent workforce/career-learning exposure, with LINC more vocational and employer-partner oriented. NNI is the underfollowed supplier/platform candidate: not an online university, but its education technology and payments segment sits inside the institutional tuition-payment and education-services workflow.
